notes_on_rating: Pre-departure collection fits every theft hypothesis, and a scientist taking a copy of her own work before leaving also fits H4. H3 says the resignation is a coincidence, so it neither predicts nor rules out this item. Weakly diagnostic on its own.

H4 rated C on purpose: by itself, an unapproved remote tool calling overseas could be shadow IT (for example, a researcher working with overseas collaborators). Item 6 is what rules that out. H2 and H5 say nothing about the tool, so NA.

H4 rated I: the credentials were used from a never-before-seen device two days after the email was opened, which goes against 'the phishing email was not acted on maliciously' (assumption A4: the device has not been verified as a new personal device). Spear-phishing senior scientists with a journal-portal lure fits both H1 and H3.

H3 rated I: criminals send stolen data to infrastructure they control, not to an employee's named personal cloud account on her own workstation. H4 rated C because the scenario itself gives a 'policy-violating personal backup habit' as a possible innocent explanation, which item 9 then undermines.

evidence_item: 5. No extortion contact or leak-site activity
notes_on_rating: Only H3 predicts extortion or resale. The I is soft: this is absence of evidence over a short window, and some criminals hold data or sell it quietly. Espionage actors and insiders do not normally extort.

evidence_item: 6. C2 infrastructure overlap with known APT
notes_on_rating: Most diagnostic item for the technical side. It is the only item that says who runs the RAT, and it contradicts both a criminal operator (H3) and an innocent tool (H4). Caveat: one SSL-certificate match, attributed with moderate confidence by a second vendor, and certificates can be shared, reused, or planted as a false flag. H2 and H5 do not address the RAT, so NA.

Feels incriminating but discriminates almost nothing. Moving to a rival is ordinary (H4), a career step (H2), a recruitment route (H1), and the beneficiary under H5. 'Same general region' is too vague to tie the firm to item 2. Close to non-diagnostic.

An enabling condition that explains how she reached the files, not why. The ACL fault started about six weeks ago, before the phishing (about three weeks), so the intruder did not create it. Non-diagnostic.

Most diagnostic item for the insider side. H4 rated I: a personal backup of her own work would not include another project's manufacturing-cost and supply-chain files. H2 rated C only because H2 covers data 'useful at her new employer'; commercial cost data from someone else's project fits directed collection (H1, H5) more naturally than career self-interest. H3 does not involve her download, so NA.

A small footprint (one phished account plus the insider) fits a low-and-slow APT and also a lone insider. H3 rated I (soft): double-extortion crews usually move laterally and escalate privileges before stealing data. H4 rated C because 'nothing widespread' is what a false alarm looks like. The phished account's anomaly was already counted under item 3.

Consistent with H1, H3 and H4 (Aurora caught up in a broad wave), so it confirms little. It also lowers the weight of item 3: Aurora was probably not singled out, which makes the timing of the phishing next to the resignation more plausibly coincidental.

evidence_item: E12 [ADDED, derived inference from items 2+4]: Exfiltration channel divergence: insider data left through a DLP-visible personal cloud account, not through the RAT/C2 channel already in the division
notes_on_rating: Student's own derived row, not a scenario fact. H1 rated I only against its coordinated-insider version: a state service with a working implant in the division would not usually have its asset upload through a traceable personal account. The I is soft, because services sometimes keep insiders and implants separate on purpose. H3 rated NA to avoid counting item 4 twice.
The tally informs but does not decide. H2 and H5 reach 0 partly because they are NA on the four technical items they do not explain. H4's three Is carry more weight than H3's four.
